paper_metadata.title: Quantum state preparation for multivariate functions

summary: The paper introduces gate-based algorithms for preparing quantum states encoding multivariate functions using Fourier or Chebyshev series with resource scaling O(d^D + Dn log d) or O(d^D + Ddn log n). Simulations demonstrate preparation of functions such as a 2D Ricker wavelet and Student’s t-distribution, while a hardware experiment prepares a 512×512 discretized Gaussian distribution on the Quantinuum H2‑1 processor using 24 qubits and up to 237 two‑qubit gates, achieving fidelities up to 0.986.

experiments.description: Preparation of a 2D Ricker wavelet on a grid using a Chebyshev-series-based gate model, with numerical simulation and resource scaling analysis.

algorithm.variant: Multivariate state preparation via truncated Chebyshev series and LCU/block-encoding

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Amplitudes encode a discretized 2D function on an equidistant grid; Chebyshev basis functions are block-encoded and combined with LCU.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Prepare a quantum state proportional to the discretized Ricker wavelet f(x,y) on [−1,1]^2.
problem_formulation.num_ancilla_qubits: D(⌈log2(d+1)⌉+⌈log2 n⌉) for Chebyshev approach; for the 2D case with D=2 this is 2(⌈log2(d+1)⌉+⌈log2 n⌉)

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Chebyshev interpolation on [−1,1]^2; coefficients computed via 2D cosine transform / FFT.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Noiseless simulation; compare prepared amplitudes to target function and report maximum absolute error and gate counts across degrees and grid sizes.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Chebyshev coefficients computed by interpolation using FFT / discrete cosine transform.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Rescale noiseless amplitudes for comparison to target function; compute maximum absolute error over grid and over continuous domain.

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: error decreases rapidly with degree; supergeometric convergence for analytic target

results.unit: O(dD + Ddn log n) two-qubit gates

speedup_claims.factor: O(dD + Ddn log n) two-qubit gates; qubits O(Dn + D log d)
speedup_claims.conditions: Chebyshev-series-based gate model; large n and d; compared qualitatively against prior work
speedup_claims.caveats: No explicit classical runtime baseline or end-to-end speedup is demonstrated; this is a resource-scaling claim.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(dD + Ddn log n) two-qubit gates for Chebyshev approach; qubits scale as O(Dn + D log d)
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: O(dx dy log(dx dy)) for 2D coefficient computation via FFT; more generally O(\bar d log \bar d)

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Unknown; algorithm provides resource scaling O(d^D + D d n log n) but no classical runtime comparison.
limiting_factors: No comparison with classical state preparation costs
State preparation itself is a subroutine rather than an end-to-end algorithm
Polynomial degree grows exponentially with dimension

notes: This is a gate-based trapped-ion experiment/simulation, not quantum annealing.
The paper reports compiled two-qubit gate counts and qubit counts for example settings, but not a single universal depth number for this experiment.
Paper analyzes scaling but does not claim quantum advantage; results are numerical simulations of circuit resources.

experiments.description: Preparation of a bivariate Student’s t-distribution using a Fourier-series-based gate model, with numerical simulation and resource scaling analysis.

algorithm.variant: Multivariate state preparation via truncated Fourier series and LCU/block-encoding

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Amplitudes encode a discretized 2D function on [0,1]^2; Fourier basis functions are implemented as controlled phase evolutions and combined with LCU.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Prepare a quantum state proportional to the discretized periodically extended Student’s t-distribution.
problem_formulation.num_ancilla_qubits: D⌈log2(2d+1)⌉ for Fourier approach; for the 2D case with D=2 this is 2⌈log2(2d+1)⌉

problem_instance.description: Bivariate non-standardized Student’s t-distribution with one degree of freedom, periodically extended to [−1,1]^2 for Fourier approximation.
problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Periodic extension from [0,1]^2 to [−1,1]^2; Fourier coefficients computed via FFT.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Noiseless simulation; compare prepared amplitudes to target function and report maximum absolute error and gate counts across degrees and grid sizes.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Fourier coefficients computed by interpolation / FFT after periodic extension.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Rescale noiseless amplitudes for comparison to target function; compute maximum absolute error over grid and over continuous domain.

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: error decays approximately as O(1/d) due to boundary derivative discontinuity from periodic extension

results.unit: O(dD + Dn log d) two-qubit gates

speedup_claims.factor: O(dD + Dn log d) two-qubit gates; qubits O(Dn + D log d)
speedup_claims.conditions: Fourier-series-based gate model; large n and d; compared qualitatively against prior work
speedup_claims.caveats: No explicit classical runtime baseline or end-to-end speedup is demonstrated; this is a resource-scaling claim.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(dD + Dn log d) two-qubit gates for Fourier approach; qubits scale as O(Dn + D log d)
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: O(Dd^D log d) for coefficient computation in the general multivariate case; for 2D FFT specifically O(dx dy log(dx dy))

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Not quantified; algorithm complexity O(d^D + D n log d) but no classical baseline.
limiting_factors: State preparation overhead remains large for high dimension
Fourier approximation error depends on function smoothness

notes: This is a gate-based Fourier-series state-preparation experiment/simulation, not quantum annealing.
The paper reports compiled two-qubit gate counts and qubit counts for example settings, but not a single universal depth number for this experiment.
Experiment evaluates approximation accuracy and gate counts only.

experiments.description: Preparation of single-electron wavefunctions in a periodic 3D Coulomb potential using the Fourier-based gate model, with numerical simulation and compilation resource estimates.

algorithm.variant: State preparation of plane-wave coefficients for a 3D electronic wavefunction via Fourier-series LCU/block-encoding

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Wavefunction amplitudes are encoded on a 3D grid; Fourier coefficients from the Schrödinger equation are loaded into ancilla registers and combined with controlled basis-function unitaries.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Prepare ground and first-excited-state wavefunctions of a single electron in a periodic Coulomb potential.
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: Electronic Hamiltonian in plane-wave basis: H^(el)_{k,k'} = -T_{k,k'} - U_{k,k'}
problem_formulation.num_ancilla_qubits: 3a where a=⌈log2 N⌉ per dimension; total ancillas = 3a

problem_instance.description: Single electron in a 3D translationally invariant Coulomb potential in a unit cell with one nucleus at the center.
problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Solve the time-independent Schrödinger equation in a plane-wave basis to obtain Fourier coefficients; then prepare the corresponding wavefunction state.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Statevector simulation compared to direct numerical evaluation of the wavefunction; compilation resource table reported for multiple n and coefficient-register sizes.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Solve the Schrödinger equation in the plane-wave basis to obtain Fourier coefficients.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Compare simulated probability density to direct numerical evaluation; report resource counts in Table 2.

speedup_claims.factor: O(dD + Dn log d) two-qubit gates; qubits O(Dn + D log d)
speedup_claims.baseline_method: classical plane-wave coefficient computation / prior quantum state-preparation methods
speedup_claims.conditions: 3D periodic Coulomb potential; Fourier-series-based state preparation
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper reports statevector simulation and compiled resource counts, not a classical runtime comparison.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(dD + Dn log d) two-qubit gates for Fourier approach; qubits scale as O(Dn + D log d)
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: Solving the Schrödinger equation in a plane-wave basis is classical preprocessing; no explicit asymptotic complexity stated for this specific instance

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Unclear; preparation cost dominated by loading Fourier coefficients O(d^D).
limiting_factors: Only simulation and compiled resource estimates
Small system (single electron in toy periodic cell)
State preparation is not the computational bottleneck in full quantum chemistry algorithms

notes: This is a gate-based quantum-simulation/state-preparation application, not quantum annealing.
The paper reports total qubits and compiled two-qubit gate counts in Table 2, but not a single depth number for this experiment.
Paper uses this example to illustrate applicability to physics simulations but does not claim advantage.

experiments.description: Hardware demonstration of preparing a 2D Gaussian distribution on Quantinuum H2-1 using a Fourier-series-based gate circuit, for both uncorrelated and correlated cases.

algorithm.variant: Multivariate state preparation via truncated Fourier series and LCU/block-encoding on hardware

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Two-dimensional function on [0,1]^2 encoded in amplitudes; Fourier coefficients loaded into ancilla registers and applied to a 2D grid state.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Prepare a quantum state proportional to a 2D Gaussian density (uncorrelated or correlated).

problem_instance.description: Uncorrelated and correlated bivariate Gaussian distributions on [0,1]^2.
problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Fourier coefficients computed analytically from the Gaussian characteristic function after extending the density to zero outside [0,1]^2; output analyzed via kernel density estimation.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: 20,000 shots per experiment; compare measured distributions to target via KDE, marginal distributions, mean/variance/correlation, and classical fidelity.

quantum_resources.readout_fidelity: State preparation and measurement error typically 0.2% on average

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Fourier coefficients computed analytically; kernel density estimation used to analyze measured data.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Post-select on ancilla zero state; estimate densities with KDE; compute marginals, means, variances, correlation coefficients, and fidelity.

speedup_claims.caveats: This is a hardware demonstration of state preparation quality, not a speedup study.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(dD + Dn log d) two-qubit gates for Fourier approach; qubits scale as O(Dn + D log d)
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: Coefficient computation from analytic characteristic function; no explicit asymptotic complexity stated for this specific experiment

advantage_assessment.crossover_size: Unknown; classical Gaussian sampling and evaluation are trivial.
advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Would require large fault‑tolerant systems where state preparation is amortized inside larger algorithms.
limiting_factors: Circuit depth limited to a few hundred gates

notes: This is the only true hardware experiment in the paper; it is gate-based on Quantinuum H2-1, not annealing.
The paper reports separate resource counts for uncorrelated and correlated Gaussian settings; both are included in one experiment because they share the same algorithm and hardware setup.
Paper demonstrates feasibility of state preparation on hardware but does not claim performance advantage.

experiments.description: Hardware demonstration of 2D Gaussian state preparation using the Fourier-series LCU method on the Quantinuum H2-1 trapped-ion quantum processor.

algorithm.variant: Multivariate Fourier-series state preparation via LCU/block-encoding

key_results: Executed on Quantinuum H2-1 with 24 qubits
Circuits used 80 two-qubit gates (uncorrelated Gaussian) and 237 two-qubit gates (correlated Gaussian)
Achieved classical fidelity F = 0.986 for uncorrelated Gaussian and F = 0.918 for correlated Gaussian
